LESSON: EARLY CIVILISATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationships
Topic 2.2: Early Civilisation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Early Civilisation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How has early African civilisation influenced the world today?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. appreciate the contribution of ancient kingdoms to the development of the modern world

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: EARLY CIVILISATION
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Early Civilisation helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: EARLY CIVILISATION
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Appreciate the contribution of ancient kingdoms to the development of the modern world

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the contribution of ancient kingdoms to the development of the modern world. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the contribution of ancient kingdoms to the development of the modern world.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Early Civilisation” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the contribution of ancient kingdoms to the development of the modern world. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Early Civilisation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Early Civilisation” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: appreciate the contribution of ancient kingdoms to the development of the modern world)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Early Civilisation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: appreciate the contribution of ancient kingdoms to the development of the modern world.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Early Civilisation from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Early Civilisation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Early Civilisation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How has early African civilisation influenced the world today?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Early Civilisation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: appreciate the contribution of ancient kingdoms to the development of the modern world.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
